verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light burning all night —
nobody home to switch it off, nobody home to notice.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A moth keeps circling the empty bulb —
somewhere a door opens
to let the spring air in.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I sweep the doorstep clean of moth-wings—
not grief exactly, just
the small work that keeps my hands from asking why.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Down the lane a child kicks a can—
its clatter says nothing
but the whole street turns to listen.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off on its own—
steam finding the window
before I've decided what I'm making.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's radio drifts from a passing car—
half a song, gone
before I catch the singer's name.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's cat pauses mid-step, staring at nothing—
I stop too, follow its gaze
into the ordinary air, finding only air.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A moth taps twice against the porch light—
then gives up,
settling on the dark side of the bulb.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I forgot the milk again—
third time this week,
the fridge humming its one complaint.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain starts before I reach the corner—
no umbrella,
just my hand doing its useless best as a hat.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's porch light clicks off at nine—
somewhere a switch decides
the day is done with us.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Traffic light holds red for no one—
the street empty,
but it waits anyway, patient as a promise.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's dog barks twice, then stops—
as if remembering
it had nowhere to be either.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A puddle keeps the shape of the sky—
even broken,
it holds what fell into it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The vending machine hums in the empty hall—
still warming something
no one's coming to choose.
